title: the coast road Rising
premise: Beatrix Pemberton, once the conservatory's most celebrated young composer, returns two decades after a public breakdown to work as its night janitor, hiding behind a smile that ends conversations. When a radio broadcast airs a song she wrote and never recorded — a piece her family buried along with the truth of what happened to her sister Iris — Beatrix realizes someone in the family has been profiting from stolen memory. As the conservatory's demolition date approaches, she quietly investigates who sold the song and why, uncovering that her father orchestrated both the theft and her disgrace to protect his legacy. In the end, Beatrix chooses justice outside the law: rather than sue or expose them, she performs the unfinished second movement at the demolition itself, reclaiming the music publicly and letting the family's arranged silence collapse on camera.
about_author: E. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the papers of defunct musical institutions. They write literary fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She begins her first week as a night janitor at the conservatory where she was once a prodigy, navigating former colleagues' awkward recognition with practiced deflection. Emotional beat: controlled numbness masking grief.

chapters.title: Static Between Stations
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Alone in the practice halls at 2 a.m., a late-night radio program plays a melody she wrote at nineteen and never recorded — her sister Iris's favorite. Emotional beat: the floor drops out; the past becomes present tense.

chapters.title: What the Family Arranged
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with flashback. She reconstructs the family's unspoken pact: never speak of Iris, never perform the unfinished work, never ask how her father's foundation grew so fast. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A posted notice gives the conservatory ninety days before demolition for her father's redevelopment project. The building that holds every memory is now on a clock. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening purpose.

chapters.title: Night Shift Confessions
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Beatrix and Marisol, the day-shift janitor who remembers the scandal differently than the newspapers told it. Marisol reveals staff whispers about a locked archive room. Emotional beat: first allyship; cautious trust.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Using an old student key she kept, Beatrix enters the sealed archive and finds her own juvenilia catalogued under her father's foundation's name — including the unreleased song's manuscript, dated after her breakdown. Emotional beat: violation turning to fury.

chapters.title: Brother at the Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Beatrix and her brother Alistair, now the foundation's director. He visits the conservatory, all charm, warning her not to 'relapse.' Their exchange is cordial warfare. Emotional beat: the mask slipping on both sides.

chapters.title: Iris, In Fragments
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, interwoven with memory chapters of Iris — brilliant, unstable, the true heir to their father's ambitions. The sisters' last argument replays. Emotional beat: tenderness braided with guilt.

chapters.title: Royalties
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Following the paper trail through licensing records, she discovers the song has earned steady royalties for twenty years, paid to the foundation. Someone has been performing it. Emotional beat: cold clarity — this was business, not accident.

chapters.title: The Pianist Who Never Was
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She identifies the recording's performer: a conservatory dropout, Daniel Okafor, who vanished after one album. He now teaches piano in a neighboring town. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Daniel Okafor
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He confesses he was paid to record the piece and sworn to silence; he thought the composer was dead. His guilt has outlived his career. Emotional beat: shared wound, unlikely alliance.

chapters.title: The Father's Version
chapters.summary: Alistair's POV. Pressured by an investigative journalist sniffing around the demolition, Alistair reviews the old cover-up and feels, for the first time, doubt. Emotional beat: corruption glimpsed from inside.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Then Sixty
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With the countdown halved, she drafts a legal complaint, then burns it — lawsuits would settle into settlements and NDAs, like everything else. Emotional beat: renouncing lawful remedy.

chapters.title: The Second Movement
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the archive at night, she finishes the composition Iris inspired — the movement she abandoned at nineteen. Playing it is the first time her hands haven't shaken in years. Emotional beat: resurrection through craft.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He anonymously sends the journalist the recording contract bearing the father's signature. Alistair scrambles; the foundation's board stirs. Emotional beat: the machine beginning to eat itself.

chapters.title: Family Dinner
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Summoned to the family estate, she faces her father — diminished by stroke but still commanding — and asks the question the whole family arranged itself around: what happened the night Iris died? He answers, finally. Emotional beat: devastating catharsis.

chapters.title: What Happened the Night Iris Died
chapters.summary: Father's fragmented POV via dictation tape. Iris confronted him about stealing Beatrix's work; the confrontation ended in the stairwell fall he blamed on Beatrix's 'instability.' Emotional beat: the founding lie exposed.

chapters.title: Alistair's Choice
chapters.summary: Alistair's POV. Offered the chance to bury the tape, he instead hands it to the journalist — choosing his niece's memory over his inheritance. Emotional beat: redemption, costly and incomplete.

chapters.title: Demolition Eve
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The story breaks; the foundation collapses; permits freeze. But the wrecking crews are already staged. Beatrix requests — and is denied — permission to enter the hall one last time. Emotional beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: The Coast Road Rising
chapters.summary: Climax. Beatrix's POV. At dawn she walks the coast road to the conservatory, past barricades, and plays the completed second movement on the hall's dying piano as crowds and cameras gather outside. Emotional beat: transfiguration; grief made public and whole.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The inquiry reopens Iris's case; the conservatory's facade is preserved as a memorial; Daniel records the piece properly, credited to B. Pemberton. Beatrix declines interviews. Emotional beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Coda: The Smile, Undone
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Months later, teaching a free Saturday class in the preserved hall, she meets a frightened prodigy and — for the first time — lets the smile drop into something real. Emotional beat: arrival; the conversation finally begins.
